newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan puts planes on standby for Cambodia pullout.
newsitem.headline: Japan puts planes on standby for Cambodia pullout.

text.p: Japan sent three military aircraft to its southernmost air base of Okinawa on Wednesday to stand by for a possible evacuation of its citizens from war-torn Cambodia, a government spokesman announced.

Spokesman Teijiro Furukawa said about 410 Japanese -- 290 residents and 120 tourists -- were stranded in Cambodia, where fighting has broken out between forces of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

But Furukawa told a news conference that unless the security situation deteriorated, evacuation of Japanese nationals was most likely to be carried out by Thai military flights already flying to Phnom Penh or by commercial planes, now that the Cambodian capital's airport has reopened.

He said in case swifter evacuation was needed, three Hercules C-130 transport planes had been sent to the Okinawan capital of Naha from Tokyo, because that was the quickest jumping off point for flights to Phnom Penh.
A flight from Naha to Phnom Penh takes about six-and-half hours, about four hours less than a direct flight from Tokyo.
If the flights go ahead, it will be the first time since World War Two that Japan, Cambodia's biggest aid donor, has sent its own military aircraft to evacuate Japanese nationals abroad.
In previous global crises, Japanese have been flown out in multinational evacuations by other nations.

In the only report so far of a foreigner killed in the Cambodian fighting, a Japanese engineer died on Sunday after his office-home was hit by a rocket at the height of weekend clashes between the rival forces in Phnom Penh.
